sentences.sentence: The NHS says that in most cases chest pain is not caused by a heart problem.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Common causes that do not involve the heart include heartburn or indigestion, a strained chest muscle, anxiety or panic, and chest infections such as pneumonia or pleurisy.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Shingles can also cause chest pain, often with a skin rash.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The main heart-related causes are angina, heart attack and pericarditis.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Pericarditis is inflammation of the lining around the heart, and the NHS says it often follows a viral infection such as a cold or flu.
sentences.note: Summary: pericarditis inflammation of heart lining, often follows viral infection like cold or flu.

sentences.sentence: Angina is chest pain that comes and goes because blood flow to the heart is reduced, and it is often triggered by physical effort or stress.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Angina attacks usually last less than 10 minutes.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says chest pain is the most common sign of a heart attack, but symptoms vary: the pain is often severe, though some people have only minor pain similar to indigestion.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Other signs include pain spreading to the arms, jaw, neck or back, sweating, breathlessness and feeling or being sick, and some people have these without any chest pain.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Unlike the pain of angina, the symptoms of a heart attack are not usually relieved by a nitrate tablet or spray.
sentences.note: Summary 'key distinction' line; page attribution to the heart attack page not exact.

sentences.sentence: A heart attack has similar symptoms but is more serious and needs emergency treatment.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales says angina is usually caused by coronary heart disease, in which narrowed or blocked arteries reduce the blood supply to the heart.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to call 999 for sudden chest pain that does not ease, or pain that spreads to the arm, jaw, neck or back.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Chest pain that comes with sweating, nausea, light-headedness or breathlessness is in the same group.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says a person with these symptoms should not drive themselves to A&E.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For someone already diagnosed with angina, the NHS treats pain that does not settle after rest or after their usual angina medicine as an emergency that needs a 999 call.
sentences.note: Summary: for people with angina pain not settling after rest or medicine is an emergency; call 999 if symptoms persist.

sentences.sentence: For sharp or stabbing chest pain that changes with breathing, swallowing, coughing or lying down, the NHS suggests an urgent GP appointment or help from NHS 111.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS also advises getting help from NHS 111 for angina that is getting worse, happening more often or coming on at rest.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says a GP who thinks a person has angina will refer them to a specialist.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Tests can include an electrocardiogram (ECG), blood tests, blood oxygen tests or scans.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An ECG records the heart's electrical activity.
sentences.note: Plain textbook definition.

sentences.sentence: An NHS emergency department leaflet says staff check for serious causes such as a heart attack, a blood clot in the lung and a collapsed lung.
sentences.note: Search summary for hospital assessment cited trust leaflets; this leaflet is among those returned; not confirmed which leaflet carried it.

sentences.sentence: The same leaflets describe troponin blood tests, which may be repeated, together with a chest X-ray or an ECG.
sentences.note: As above; blended summary of trust leaflets.

sentences.sentence: A normal first troponin result lowers the chance of a heart problem but does not rule it out.
sentences.note: As above; blended summary of trust leaflets.

sentences.sentence: For a heart attack, the blood tests look for troponin, a protein released when heart muscle is damaged, and further tests can include an echocardiogram and a coronary angiogram, which shows where blood flow is blocked.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A heart attack is treated in hospital, and options include medicines to clear blockages, angioplasty with a stent, and bypass surgery.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says the aims of angina treatment are to relieve symptoms, prevent further attacks, and reduce the risk of a heart attack or stroke.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Medicines include GTN for attacks and beta blockers or calcium channel blockers to prevent them, and surgery may be recommended to improve blood flow to the heart.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Lifestyle changes the NHS lists for angina include a balanced diet, cutting down on alcohol, stopping smoking and losing weight if overweight.
sentences.note: Summary of angina lifestyle section.
